title: Roll-up summary fields and alternatives
objectives: Define a roll-up summary field as a custom field on the master that aggregates detail records in a master-detail relationship.
Choose COUNT, SUM, MIN, or MAX and name which child field types each operation allows.
Refuse a roll-up when the relationship is lookup, when the input is a cross-object formula, or when the need is a formula display on the child.
Name alternatives (declarative automation, Apex, reporting) without inventing unofficial product limits.
diagnostic_question: Property should show a count of units and the latest inspection date. Units are master-detail; inspections are lookup. Which number can be a roll-up summary field, and what do you do for the other?
definition: A roll-up summary field is a custom field on the master object that aggregates values from detail records in a master-detail relationship. Create it on the master; choose the detail object and an operation: COUNT of related records; SUM of number, currency, or percent fields; MIN or MAX of number, currency, percent, date, or date/time fields. If the relationship does not exist, create the master-detail first. You cannot reference cross-object formulas in roll-up summary fields. ([Create a Roll-Up Summary Field](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_defining_summary_fields.htm); [Custom Field Attributes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm); [Tips for Building Cross-Object Formulas](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers bait you into rolling up a lookup child or a spanning formula. Native roll-ups require master-detail and allowed field types. The alternative is not 'a formula that queries children' (DATA-006)—it is a different relationship, automation, or a report.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a warehouse tally board bolted to the pallet. It can count, sum, or show min/max only for boxes glued to that pallet (master-detail). Loose consulting notes sitting nearby (lookup inspections) do not move the tally. You cannot feed a reprint formula that already walked to another warehouse into this board. If the boxes are not glued, you need another counter: automation, Apex, or a report—not a fake formula COUNT.
deeper_explanation: Help: define the roll-up on the object on the master side. If no relationship exists, create a master-detail between the master that displays the value and the detail that contains the records. Then choose COUNT, SUM, MIN, or MAX and optional filter criteria. ([Create a Roll-Up Summary Field](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_defining_summary_fields.htm))

Custom Field Attributes: SUM allows number, currency, and percent. MIN and MAX also allow date and date/time. COUNT totals related records. Calculation options include automatic recalculation when displayed and a force mass recalculation safety net. ([Custom Field Attributes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm))

Master-detail rules from DATA-003 still apply: cascade delete, no Owner on detail, inherited sharing. Do not convert a lookup to master-detail only to get a roll-up if the child must remain independent. That is when you name an alternative.

Cross-object formulas cannot be roll-up inputs. Formula fields cannot replace child aggregates. Numeric roll-up limits (how many per object) are edition- and release-sensitive—Needs verification in current Help; do not invent a number.

Alternatives when native roll-up does not fit: a report or dashboard summary; record-triggered Flow or Apex that maintains a stored number (DATA-005 writer); or changing grain to a true master-detail if life cycle allows. Mark Flow/Apex mechanics as neighboring AUTO/APEX topics.

mental_model.analogy: A tally board bolted to a pallet that only counts boxes glued to that pallet (master-detail), not loose notes on the floor (lookup).
useful_mapping: roll-up field → tally board on the master pallet
filter criteria → count only red boxes
lookup children → loose notes the board will not tally
cross-object formula → a reprint from another warehouse the board cannot ingest
alternative → a clerk (Flow/Apex) or a printed report if boxes are not glued
where_it_breaks: Recalculation timing is not a person with a clipboard; use Help's automatic vs mass-recalc options.
Junction objects can be details of two masters; which side gets which roll-up needs care.
Unofficial 'max roll-ups per object' numbers are not quoted here.
The analogy does not encode sharing or skew from 10,000 children (DATA-005).

when_to_use: When a master object must show COUNT, SUM, MIN, or MAX of master-detail children.
When the child field type matches the roll-up operation (for example Date for MAX latest date).
When you want the platform to maintain the aggregate without a handwritten stamp.
When filter criteria should include only some detail records in the summary.
When explaining why a lookup child cannot use a native roll-up summary field.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a roll-up summary field on a lookup relationship; change the relationship only if DATA-003 life cycle allows.
Do not roll up a cross-object formula field.
Do not use a roll-up when you need a parent value displayed on the child (that is a formula field).
Do not use a roll-up as a validation rule or error message (DATA-010).
Do not convert thousands of independent children to master-detail just to get a count (DATA-005 skew and Owner loss).

decision_table.signal: Need a count or sum of master-detail children on the parent.

decision_table.not: A formula field on the master that queries children.

interview_questions.question: What is a roll-up summary field?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A custom field on the master that aggregates master-detail children with COUNT, SUM, MIN, or MAX. It is not a formula that queries children and not a lookup feature.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I place it on the parent. I confirm MD and allowed types. I mention optional filters and recalc options. I refuse lookup children and spanning-formula inputs. I name alternatives without converting life cycle just for a tally.
interview_questions.example: LAB_UnitCount__c COUNT on LAB_Property__c summarizing LAB_Unit__c.

interview_questions.question: Latest inspection date on Property when inspections are lookup?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Native roll-up is ineligible. Keep lookup if inspections need Owner. Use a report or a maintained stored date via Flow or Apex.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not convert inspections to MD just for MAX. That would cascade-delete audits and remove queues. I document the alternative owner. I do not write a Property formula that pretends to MAX children.
interview_questions.example: Design note: LAB_LastInspection__c maintained by Flow, not a roll-up.
follow_ups: What if we later make inspections MD?
weak_answer_warnings: Converting to MD in the interview without life-cycle talk

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse a roll-up even if MD exists?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the input is a cross-object formula, when the child type is wrong for the operation, or when 10,000-child skew makes a maintained aggregate dangerous without a volume plan.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still like native roll-ups for honest MD children. I check SUM types. I check DATA-005 volume. I do not roll up a spanning city formula. I mention mass recalc as a sandbox tool after filter changes.
interview_questions.example: Rejected rolling up Inspection.LAB_PropertyCity__c formula even if someone later made inspections MD.
follow_ups: When do you force mass recalc?
weak_answer_warnings: Always saying yes if MD exists

interview_questions.question: Compare formula fields and roll-up summary fields.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Formulas calculate from the same row or parents. Roll-ups aggregate children onto the master. Formulas do not COUNT children. Roll-ups cannot ingest cross-object formulas.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Direction is the interview gold. City on inspection is a formula. Unit count on property is a roll-up. I mention return type vs roll-up operation. I keep validation rules out of both.
interview_questions.example: LAB_PropertyCity__c formula on Inspection vs LAB_UnitCount__c roll-up on Property.
follow_ups: Can a same-object formula be rolled up?
Can a roll-up be used in a formula?

interview_questions.question: The roll-up wizard does not list Inspection as a summarized object.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Inspection is not a master-detail child of this master. The wizard only summarizes MD details.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open Fields & Relationships on Inspection and confirm lookup vs MD. I do not recreate Property. I either change the model with a life-cycle review or pick an alternative. I also confirm I started the field on the master, not the child.
interview_questions.example: Inspection.Property__c is lookup, so it never appears in Property's roll-up summarized-object list.
tradeoffs: Wrong object vs wrong field type
follow_ups: What if there are two MD parents?
weak_answer_warnings: Toggling the browser and retrying the wizard only

interview_questions.question: SUM of unit square footage is missing the field in the picker.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: LAB_SqFt__c is probably Text or a spanning formula. SUM needs number, currency, or percent on the detail.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I inspect the child field type (DATA-002). I convert or replace the field in sandbox if data allows. I do not SUM a text '1200'. I do not change the roll-up to COUNT and call it done if they needed area.
interview_questions.example: Recreated LAB_SqFt__c as Number; SUM then appeared.
tradeoffs: Convert type vs new number field
follow_ups: Can you SUM a currency field?

interview_questions.question: Filtered COUNT of occupied units—how?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A roll-up summary with filter criteria on the occupied checkbox, not a second object.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I create COUNT on Property, summarized object Unit, filter LAB_Occupied__c equals true. If the org is multilingual I enter filter values in the default language as Help says. I test occupied and vacant LAB_ units.
interview_questions.example: LAB_OccupiedUnitCount__c COUNT where Occupied is true.
follow_ups: Do you need mass recalc after changing the filter?
Can you filter on a spanning formula?
weak_answer_warnings: Creating OccupiedUnit__c as a new object

interview_questions.question: What alternatives do you name when native roll-up does not fit?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A report or dashboard for read-only totals; a stored number maintained by Flow or Apex when the value must live on the record; or a relationship change only if cascade and Owner are acceptable.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat alternatives as first-class interview content. I do not endorse a specific AppExchange package. I do not pretend a formula COUNT exists. I mention AUTO-001 and APEX topics own the automation mechanics. I warn about writers and skew if we stamp a number on a hot parent.
interview_questions.example: Weekly inspection report plus optional Flow increment on Property.LAB_InspectionCount__c.
follow_ups: Who recalculates after a data fix?
How do you prevent double-count in Flow?
